title: The Forged Ledger
story: A ledger holds six memos. Only memos stamped VERIFIED are genuine. Forgeries are everywhere.
instructions: Only clues marked VERIFIED can be trusted. Ignore every UNVERIFIED clue. Enter the six-digit code; leading zeros count.

clues.text: [VERIFIED] The first pair is the number of letters in VAULT, multiplied by 3.
[UNVERIFIED] The first pair is 51.
[VERIFIED] The middle pair is two to the power of five.
[UNVERIFIED] The last digit is 9.
[VERIFIED] The last pair is the middle pair minus the first pair.
[UNVERIFIED] The middle pair is a multiple of 7.

hints: Ignore every memo that is not stamped VERIFIED.
Compute 5 x 3, then 2^5, then subtract.
Near the end: the code starts with 15 and ends with 7. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Shifted Letters
story: A cryptogram is scratched into the wall: HIGMHI.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Each letter of HIGMHI was moved forward 4 places in the alphabet. Undo the shift to reveal a word.
Then replace each letter by its position in the alphabet (A = 1 ... I = 9). The result is the code.

explanation: HIGMHI shifted back by 4 is DECIDE. D=4, E=5, C=3, I=9, D=4, E=5: 453945. The code is 453945.
steps: HIGMHI shifted back by 4 is DECIDE.
hints: Shift each letter back by four.
H goes back to D. Do the same for the rest.
Near the end: the code starts with 45 and ends with 5. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Mixed Bases
story: Three numbers in three number systems are carved over the door.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: octal 77, converted to ordinary decimal.
Middle pair: hexadecimal 2A, converted to decimal.
Last pair: binary 11001, converted to decimal.

hints: Each digit position is worth a power of the base.
Near the end: the code starts with 63 and ends with 5. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Hidden in Plain Sight
story: The guard's message looks innocent. Count carefully.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The guard says: "Is it a very hidden answer?" The code is the number of letters in each word, in order.

hints: The message has exactly six words.
Count the letters of each word separately. Ignore punctuation.
Near the end: the code starts with 22 and ends with 6. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Growing Gaps
story: The wall shows 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 17 and then stops.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The gaps between neighbouring terms form a pattern of their own. The code is the next three terms as pairs.

hints: Write down the differences between terms.
The differences are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. What comes next?
Near the end: the code starts with 23 and ends with 8. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Three Guards
story: Three guards each make a statement about the first two digits. Exactly one of them is lying.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Guard 1: "The first digit is 3."
Guard 2: "The second digit is 5."
Guard 3: "The first two digits add up to 9."
Exactly one of the three guards lies.
The first digit is even.
The third digit is the last digit of the product of the first two.
The fourth digit is the sum of the first two digits.
The last two digits form the square of the second digit.

explanation: Even first digit means Guard 1 lies. Guards 2 and 3 are honest: second digit 5, sum 9, so the first digit is 4. Third digit: 20 -> 0. Fourth: 9. Last two: 25. Code: 450925. The code is 450925.
steps: Even first digit means Guard 1 lies. Guards 2 and 3 are honest: second digit 5, sum 9, so the first digit is 4.
hints: If the first digit is even, what does that say about Guard 1?
Guard 1 must be the liar, so Guards 2 and 3 tell the truth.
Near the end: the code starts with 45 and ends with 5. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Symbol Swap
story: Four glyphs stand for four different single-digit numbers.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The code is the glyph sequence ■ ◆ ▲ ● ● ◆ translated into digits.

hints: Solve ◆ first: three of them make 9.
◆ = 3, so ▲ = 5. Then ● and ■ follow.
Near the end: the code starts with 73 and ends with 3. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Mini Sudoku
story: A 4 x 4 grid must hold 1 to 4 in every row, column and 2 x 2 box.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Fill the blanks (_) so every row, every column and every 2 x 2 box contains 1, 2, 3 and 4 once.
The code is the six blanks read column by column, each column top to bottom, columns left to right.

explanation: Solution grid rows: 1234 / 3412 / 2143 / 4321. Reading blanks by column: 3 | 2, 3 | 4 | 4, 2. Code: 323442. The code is 323442.
hints: Start with the row that has two blanks and the column that constrains them.
Row 1 needs 2 and 4, but the 4 in column 2 forbids 4 in the second cell.
Near the end: the code starts with 32 and ends with 2. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Order of Operations
story: The vault applies multiplication before addition, and the rules matter.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: 8 + 4 x 3.
Middle pair: (8 + 4) x 3.
Last pair: 2 + 3^2 x 2 - 4 / 2.

hints: Brackets first, then powers, then multiplication and division, then addition and subtraction.
Near the end: the code starts with 20 and ends with 8. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Digit Chain
story: Each digit depends on the ones before it.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The first digit is the number of vertices of a tetrahedron.
The second digit is twice the first digit, minus 3.
The third digit is the remainder when the sum of the first two digits is divided by 7.
The fourth digit is the last digit of the second digit times the third digit.
The fifth digit is the difference between the first and fourth digits (ignoring sign) plus the third digit.
The last digit is the last digit of the sum of all five earlier digits.

hints: A tetrahedron has 4 corners. Build from the left.
4, then 2 x 4 - 3 = 5, then (4 + 5) mod 7.
Near the end: the code starts with 45 and ends with 7. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Hit Count
story: A code-breaking machine logged earlier attempts. Each shows how many digits were correct AND in the right place.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The code uses six different digits.
Attempt 1: 876543  ->  2 digits are in the right place.
Attempt 2: 706239  ->  1 digit is in the right place.
Attempt 3: 370516  ->  1 digit is in the right place.
Attempt 4: 071923  ->  2 digits are in the right place.
Attempt 5: 946385  ->  0 digits are in the right place.
Attempt 6: 420673  ->  1 digit is in the right place.
Attempt 7: 134620  ->  1 digit is in the right place.
Attempt 8: 547690  ->  0 digits are in the right place.
Attempt 9: 019427  ->  0 digits are in the right place.
Attempt 10: 534268  ->  1 digit is in the right place.
Attempt 11: 830456  ->  1 digit is in the right place.
Attempt 12: 650712  ->  1 digit is in the right place.

explanation: The code consistent with every attempt is 804913. Eliminate digits per position using the 0-hit attempts, then count hits in the others. The code is 804913.
steps: The code consistent with every attempt is 804913.
Eliminate digits per position using the 0-hit attempts, then count hits in the others.
hints: Attempts with 0 hits tell you which digits are NOT in which positions.
Combine attempts: a position can only hold one digit, and all six digits differ.
Near the end: the code starts with 80 and ends with 3. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Roman Numerals
story: Roman inscriptions cover the vault walls.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: XLVII.
Middle pair: LXXXIII.
Last pair: the last two digits of the year MMXXIV.

hints: XLVII = 40 + 5 + 2. LXXXIII = 50 + 30 + 3. MMXXIV = 2000 + 24.
Near the end: the code starts with 47 and ends with 4. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Knights and Knaves
story: Six islanders (A to F) are either knights, who always tell the truth, or knaves, who always lie.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Island one. A says: "A and B are the same type." B says: "C is a knave." C says: "A is a knight."
Island two. D says: "F is a knave." E says: "D and F are the same type." F says: "E is a knight."
The code has one digit per islander, in order A to F. A knave's digit is 0. A knight's digit is the islander's place in the list (A = 1, B = 2, ... F = 6).

explanation: Island one: A knave, B knight, C knave. Island two: D knight, E knave, F knave. Digits: A=0, B=2, C=0, D=4, E=0, F=0. Code: 020400. The code is 020400.
steps: Island one: A knave, B knight, C knave. Island two: D knight, E knave, F knave.
hints: Work out island one on its own: assume A is a knight and see what happens.
Whatever A is, B turns out to be a knight. Then C is a knave, and A must be a knave too.
Near the end: the code starts with 02 and ends with 0. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Product of Pairs
story: Two sealed numbers multiply to a famous value.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: The first pair times the middle pair equals 1296.
The middle pair is four times the first pair.
The last pair is the number of positive divisors of 1296.

explanation: first^2 = 324, first = 18, middle = 72. 1296 = 2^4 x 3^4 has 5 x 5 = 25 divisors. The code is 187225.
hints: Replace the middle pair by 4 x first.
So 4 x first^2 = 1296. For divisors, factor 1296 = 6^4.
Near the end: the code starts with 18 and ends with 5. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Letter Equations
story: Six letters stand for six digits.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: B + C = 9
C + D = 8
The code is the digits of A, B, C, D, E, F in that order.

hints: F is known, so work backwards.
Near the end: the code starts with 65 and ends with 7. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Noise Filter
story: A string of random characters scrolls past: ab3de7fo2gi9hu4ij1ka5ez8pa6
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Only digits that come immediately after a vowel (a, e, i, o, u) belong to the code. Take them in order.

explanation: Digits after vowels: 7, 2, 9, 4, 5, 6. The code is 729456.
hints: Ignore digits that follow a consonant.
Scan for a vowel followed directly by a digit.
Near the end: the code starts with 72 and ends with 6. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Calculator Trail
story: The vault gives a starting number and a list of instructions.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Start with 7. Multiply by 8. That result is the first pair.
Subtract 6, then divide by 5. That result is the middle pair.
Square the middle pair, then subtract the first pair. That result is the last pair.

hints: Follow the instructions in order.
Near the end: the code starts with 56 and ends with 4. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Triangular Vault
story: Triangular numbers are 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, ... Each is the sum of 1 up to n.
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: First pair: the 8th triangular number.
Middle pair: the 10th triangular number.
Last pair: the 12th triangular number minus the 9th.

hints: The nth triangular number is n(n+1)/2.
Near the end: the code starts with 36 and ends with 3. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: Two Voices
story: Two sequences are woven together: 2, 100, 4, 90, 8, 80, 16, 70, ...
instructions: Use every clue. Single-digit answers inside a pair need a leading zero (6 becomes 06). Enter the six-digit code.

clues.text: Every other term belongs to the same sequence. The code is the next three terms as pairs.

explanation: Doubling: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. Decreasing: 100, 90, 80, 70, 60. Next terms: 32, 60, 64. The code is 326064.
hints: Separate odd-numbered terms from even-numbered terms.
One sequence doubles. The other drops by 10.
Near the end: the code starts with 32 and ends with 4. Work out the middle three digits yourself.

title: The Deceiver
story: The last gate of the chapter is guarded by a master of misdirection. Trust only what is VERIFIED.
instructions: Only clues marked VERIFIED can be trusted. Ignore every UNVERIFIED clue. Enter the six-digit code; leading zeros count.

clues.text: [VERIFIED] Undo a shift of 3 on WKUHH. The word names a number. The first pair is that number times nine.
[VERIFIED] The middle pair is binary 101101 minus the first pair.
[VERIFIED] The last pair is the number of letters in the decoded word, times the middle pair.
[UNVERIFIED] The code ends with a 5.
[UNVERIFIED] The first pair is 36.

explanation: WKUHH shifted back 3 is THREE, so the first pair is 3 x 9 = 27. 101101 is 45, so the middle pair is 45 - 27 = 18. THREE has 5 letters: 5 x 18 = 90. Code: 27 18 90. The code is 271890.
steps: WKUHH shifted back 3 is THREE, so the first pair is 3 x 9 = 27.
101101 is 45, so the middle pair is 45 - 27 = 18.
hints: Decode the word first. It names a number.
THREE is 3. Binary 101101 is 32 + 8 + 4 + 1.
Near the end: the code starts with 27 and ends with 0. Work out the middle three digits yourself.
